comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
COMPLETED: ht-tvn.5, commit df9fa99 (Bead trailer bound), review minors 1 and 2 and the nitpick of ht-tvn.4.

WHAT
1. _answers_kill_session checks urlsplit(response.url).path for /broker/xml first and returns False otherwise; only then it reads post_data for <kill-session. A non-UTF-8 POST answered during the wait no longer reaches the strict decode.
2. After the wait, _confirm_logoff_dialog logs at INFO: "Horizon kill-session answered: <status> after <ms> ms". status = answer.value.status (any status, a 401/500 releases the wait too; the fresh list decides). ms = time.monotonic() from the OK click's return to the end of the wait, rounded. The line carries only two integers: no URL, no body, no credential. The timeout path now returns after its warning (unchanged text).
3. Nit: a cheap pin exists. Fixture knob kill_session_sync sends kill-session as a synchronous XHR inside OK's click handler, so the answer is in before click() returns. Probe (scratchpad/ht-tvn.5/probe_armed.py, Chromium 1194): wait armed after the click missed the answer 100/100; armed before caught it 100/100. Not a Playwright contract, measured ordering; SPEC Testing says so.

title: [HT-002] Re-review of the kill-session wait
description: Narrow re-review of ht-tvn.3 only.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
REVIEW PASSED: ht-tvn.3 (commit 9f243d8), the log off now waits for the broker's kill-session answer before it reloads. 0 critical, 0 major, 2 minor, 1 nitpick.

Checked against the brief:
- The wait is armed before the OK click. _confirm_logoff_dialog opens page.expect_response(...) and then clicks inside the with block. In the installed Playwright, EventContextManager.__exit__ cancels the wait when the body raises, so a failed click surfaces as the click's own error.
- The bound has a name and a reason. HorizonTimeouts.kill_session_answer_ms=30_000 carries a comment saying why it exists (the credential-cleanup reload) and that the live answer time is not measured. The SPEC row, the SPEC "Confirming a log off" section, the constructor line, the constants list and the infrastructure README all say this. sync-check is ok.
- An unanswered kill-session still fails closed. On PlaywrightTimeoutError after the click, the adapter logs a warning and the fresh-list poll decides. test_a_log_off_whose_kill_session_is_never_answered_is_not_confirmed covers this: LOGOFF_NOT_CONFIRMED, a screenshot, and the session still DISCONNECTED.
- I checked the predicate against the bundle app-htmlaccess.4eb7424a56fc03317f06.js:
  - Kw.setRequestXML builds session-id, and Oi.createXML wraps it as <broker ...><kill-session>...</kill-session></broker>. So KILL_SESSION_TAG matches, including when the router batches handlers into one document.
  - jscdkPost and postMessage send it as an in-page XHR to .../broker/xml. The mid query, the _ab timestamp and the F5 suffix leave the path containing /broker/xml. The audio, video and unauth Workers do not carry broker traffic, so page.expect_response sees the request.
  - enableCredentialCleanupForHTMLAccess and waitForCredentialClean (3e3) are as the SPEC says.

Measurements (Chromium via PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers):
- Suite: 476 passed, 7 skipped. Before the fix it was 473 + 7, and the difference is the 3 new tests. The 1 warning is pytest_bdd's unknown mark "wip", which comes from the HT-003 skips and is unrelated.
- Coverage: 98.52% total; horizon_playwright.py 96%.
- ruff check src/ tests/ is clean. mypy src/ tests/ is clean over 65 files.
- Clean index (rm beadloom.db, reindex): lint --strict rc 0, sync-check rc 0, doctor rc 0.
- Secrets: the lines added in 6315ccf..HEAD (excluding .beads) contain no credential material. The one new log line carries only the bound in ms.

Sabotage. Each edit was a precise string replace, reversed the same way. The selection was 10 log-off tests in test_horizon_playwright.py (-k log_off), 10 passed at baseline, and the tree was clean after each step.
- S1, drop the wait (plain click): 7 failed, among them test_a_log_off_waits_for_the_brokers_kill_session_answer_before_reloading and ..._never_answered_is_not_confirmed.
- S1b, the pre-fix behaviour (click, then a fixed 1 s wait): 2 failed. test_a_log_off_waits_for_the_brokers_kill_session_answer_before_reloading failed with HorizonClientError logoff_not_confirmed (cut off), and ..._never_answered_ failed on its warning text. The 1.5 s answer proves the wait.
- S2, shorten the bound (FAST.kill_session_answer_ms 3_000 -> 500, below the 1.5 s answer): 2 failed. The slow-answer test failed logoff_not_confirmed, so the shortened bound fails closed. The never-answered test failed on the "3000 ms" text.
- S4, predicate fooled (any /broker/xml response, so the fixture's sibling set-last-user-activity releases the wait): 7 failed, including the slow-answer test. The fixture's decoy works.
- S5, swallow a failed OK click (drop "if not clicked: raise"): 1 failed, test_a_log_off_whose_confirmation_never_shows_fails_without_awaiting_an_answer.
- S3, arm the wait after the click: 10 passed. See the nitpick.

Minor:
1. horizon_playwright.py _answers_kill_session (lines 520-523): the predicate decodes every page response's request body before it checks the path. Request.post_data is a strict UTF-8 .decode(). I probed this in a scratch script, scratchpad/ht-tvn.4/probe_decode.py: a page POST with a non-UTF-8 body during the wait made expect_response raise a Playwright Error "'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff". That error is not PlaywrightTimeoutError. So it escapes the except, _step turns it into LOGOFF_NOT_CONFIRMED at the OK click, and the fresh-list confirmation never runs, even when the kill-session was sent. This fails closed, but any unrelated binary POST in that window (telemetry, uploads) turns it into a false failure. Recommendation: check the URL path first and read the body only for /broker/xml responses, for example "if BROKER_XML_PATH not in urlsplit(response.url).path: return False", then the tag check. A decode guard (post_data_buffer and "in" on bytes) also works.
2. The success path logs nothing. The SPEC lists "how long the broker takes to answer kill-session" as not measured. BRIEF BEAD-03 asks for it from the log ("the kill-session request leaves and gets its answer before the reload (per the journal)"). As it stands, the log can show only that the warning is absent. It cannot show the answer's status or how long it took, and the 30 s bound needs that number to be sized. Also, any status (401/500) counts as "answered". That is safe, because the fresh list decides, but nothing records it. Recommendation: after the with block, log at info "Horizon kill-session answered: <status> after <ms> ms" (event.value.status and the elapsed time). The live check (ht-28a) can then read the answer, its status and its timing from the log.

Nitpick:
- No test pins "armed before the OK click". S3 (click, then arm) passes 10/10, because the fixture's 40 ms hop and 0-1.5 s answers always come after re-arming. The code is correct as written. A regression would cost a 30 s wait and then the fresh-list decision, not a false result. A deterministic pin needs an answer that is guaranteed to arrive before Python regains control, which a localhost fixture cannot promise. If you want one anyway, a 0-hop, 0-delay mode that asserts the warning is absent in the happy path catches it most of the time. Otherwise leave it to code review.

Layering, cohesion and typing: nothing found. The adapter imports only playwright and the domain, and there is one new method with one named responsibility. Response is typed and the new code has no Any or type: ignore. The fixture-only assumptions (set-last-user-activity, the cut-off on logout) are labelled as the fixture's own in the fixture header, the test docstring and the SPEC Testing section.

Independence: review-brief --release withheld the author's account (no verdict recorded yet). I read the 9f243d8 commit body, which carries the author's framing, at the start, along with ht-tvn.2's comments. I did not read ht-tvn.3's comments.

Docs to check: docs/domains/infrastructure/features/horizon-playwright-client/SPEC.md (API, Confirming a log off, Testing), docs/domains/infrastructure/README.md (adapter row).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
COMPLETED: the log off waits for the broker's kill-session answer before it reloads the launch list (review ht-tvn.2 minor 1). Commit 9f243d8 (Bead: ht-tvn.3 trailer checked with git log %(trailers)).

What changed
- Adapter (horizon_playwright.py): the fixed poll_ms wait after OK is gone. _confirm_logoff_dialog arms page.expect_response before the OK click. It matches a response from .../broker/xml whose request body carries <kill-session>. That is the bundle's request shape, cross-checked by grep in app-htmlaccess.4eb7424a56fc03317f06.js: Kw.setRequestXML builds <session-id>; Oi.createXML wraps it in <broker version=...><kill-session>...</kill-session></broker>; jscdkPost posts it to ${brokerUrl}/broker/xml. The bound is HorizonTimeouts.kill_session_answer_ms = 30_000, with the reason in its comment. Past the bound the adapter logs "Horizon kill-session unanswered after N ms" and goes on to the fresh-list poll, which fails closed. The page is still left on a fresh list, so the check-out's second desktop_status still reads the broker. An OK click that fails is re-raised (LOGOFF_NOT_CONFIRMED at once) and is never read as "unanswered".
- Fixture JS: kill-session is a POST of a <broker> XML document to /broker/xml (it was /fixture/kill-session JSON before). OK also sends <set-last-user-activity/> to /broker/xml, answered at once, so the predicate must pick the kill-session's answer. With credential_cleanup on, the page posts <do-logout/> on beforeunload by keepalive fetch (the bundle's _sendLogoutAction, LogoutFromBroker, sendFetch). A behaviour flag logoff_dialog=false leaves the confirmation hidden.
- Fixture server (test module): /broker/xml dispatches kill-session, do-logout and set-last-user-activity. The broker acts on kill-session when it answers, after kill_session_answer_s. A logout of that web session before the answer cuts it off: event "kill-session-cut-off", session kept. kill_session_unanswered holds the request until teardown (released Event, 30 s cap). Logged-out tokens go in a set, so token minting is unchanged.
- SPEC: the confirmation paragraph says the adapter waits for the kill-session answer, then reloads; also the bound, fail-closed, the not-measured broker timing and the credential-cleanup sentence (review nitpick), API and Testing. Not-measured list updated.

Tests (TDD)
- RED first: with the field added and the adapter still on HEAD's 1-interval wait, test_a_log_off_waits_for_the_brokers_kill_session_answer_before_reloading failed with HorizonClientError logoff_not_confirmed (the reload's do-logout cut the 1.5 s kill-session off), and test_a_log_off_whose_kill_session_is_never_answered_is_not_confirmed failed on the absent "unanswered" log line.
- New tests (3): ..._waits_for_the_brokers_kill_session_answer_before_reloading (credential cleanup on, answer after 1.5 s, beyond the live 1 s the adapter once waited; asserts answered before broker-logout, no cut-off, session none, NO_SESSION after); ..._whose_kill_session_is_never_answered_is_not_confirmed (LOGOFF_NOT_CONFIRMED, screenshot, the bounded-wait log line, DISCONNECTED after); ..._whose_confirmation_never_shows_fails_without_awaiting_an_answer.
- Full suite on the final code: 476 passed, 7 skipped (HT-003 placeholders, reason printed by -rs); it was 473/7. Adapter file: 35 collected, 35 passed. comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
API CHANGE (commit 5634cb1): horizon_tracker.infrastructure.config.Settings, for BEAD-04 (ht-rat) and BEAD-05 (ht-978).

New Settings fields (all frozen, read by Settings.from_env):
- checkin_range: TimeRange (HT_CHECKIN_RANGE, HH:MM-HH:MM, default 07:30-08:10)
- checkout_range: TimeRange (HT_CHECKOUT_RANGE, default 16:30-17:10)
- session_length: timedelta (HT_SESSION_LENGTH_MINUTES, default 540)
- session_extra_max: timedelta (HT_SESSION_EXTRA_MAX_MINUTES, default 10)
- window_grace: timedelta (HT_WINDOW_GRACE_MINUTES, default 5)
- jitter_seed: bytes (HT_JITTER_SEED verbatim, UTF-8; unset or blank -> HORIZON_USERNAME in UTF-8). Masked in repr/str as '***' like username/password/token/chat id.
For BEAD-04: draw_moments(today, s.jitter_seed, s.checkin_range, s.session_length, s.session_extra_max, s.checkout_range) then window_from(moment, s.window_grace). These exact arguments are validated at load, so the draw and window_from cannot raise ValueError at run time for a Settings that exists.

Kept for now, removed in BEAD-04: checkin_window / checkout_window (Window). No variable sets them any more; they are fixed at the HT-001 values HT001_CHECKIN_WINDOW = 07:55-08:00 and HT001_CHECKOUT_WINDOW = 17:00-17:05 (module constants), so cli.py and its tests behave exactly as before. BEAD-04 deletes both fields, both constants, and the interim test test_the_cli_keeps_the_fixed_ht001_windows_until_it_draws_its_moments, and changes the probe "settings:" line (cli._echo_probe still prints these windows).

Removed: HT_CHECKIN_WINDOW and HT_CHECKOUT_WINDOW are no longer read. If either key is present in the environment (even blank), from_env raises ConfigError naming it before any other check, with a hint naming HT_CHECKIN_RANGE / HT_CHECKOUT_RANGE (+ HT_SESSION_LENGTH_MINUTES, HT_SESSION_EXTRA_MAX_MINUTES for check-out) and HT_WINDOW_GRACE_MINUTES. Removed constants: DEFAULT_CHECKIN_WINDOW, DEFAULT_CHECKOUT_WINDOW.
For BEAD-05: deploy.yml must stop writing HT_CHECKIN_WINDOW/HT_CHECKOUT_WINDOW (a .env carrying them now makes every command exit 1 with "configuration error: HT_CHECKIN_WINDOW: ...") and write the six new names; RUNBOOK .env block and tests/unit/deploy/test_units.py (WINDOW_VARIABLE regex over the RUNBOOK) likewise.

Validation at load, each refusal a ConfigError naming the variable:
- ranges: format HH:MM-HH:MM, then TimeRange (start before end, whole minutes)
- minutes: a whole number 0..1440 (bound keeps the draw away from datetime overflow; nothing in a daily schedule lasts longer than a day)
- HT_CHECKOUT_RANGE: draw_moments with the real ranges and a 1-minute session -> the domain's range-order rule; message also names HT_CHECKIN_RANGE
- HT_SESSION_LENGTH_MINUTES: draw_moments with the real session -> 0 refused
- HT_WINDOW_GRACE_MINUTES: window_from(checkout_range.end, grace) -> 0 refused, and a grace that carries the latest possible window past midnight refused
New public names: CHECKIN_RANGE, CHECKOUT_RANGE, SESSION_LENGTH, SESSION_EXTRA_MAX, WINDOW_GRACE, JITTER_SEED (variable names); DEFAULT_CHECKIN_RANGE, DEFAULT_CHECKOUT_RANGE, DEFAULT_SESSION_LENGTH_MINUTES, DEFAULT_SESSION_EXTRA_MAX_MINUTES, DEFAULT_WINDOW_GRACE_MINUTES; HT001_CHECKIN_WINDOW, HT001_CHECKOUT_WINDOW (interim).

comments.text:
API CHANGE (commit a059be6) — the horizon CLI, for BEAD-05 (ht-978, .env contract / RUNBOOK) and BEAD-08 (ht-6l0).

Commands and flags: unchanged names (checkin, checkout, probe; --dry-run, --force), unchanged exit codes (run: 1 only on a FAILED report; probe: 1 only if portal or chrome FAILED; configuration error: 1).
- checkin/checkout: each run draws today's moments: draw_moments(clock.now().date() in HT_TIMEZONE, jitter_seed, checkin_range, session_length, session_extra_max, checkout_range); its own moment -> window_from(moment, window_grace) -> WindowedRun(..., moment=moment, range_start=<its range>.start). Started in [range start, moment): one sleep until the moment, then runs. Before the range start: skipped too_early, no wait. After moment+grace: skipped window_missed. Report carries planned_at = the moment ("Time: ..., planned for HH:MM").
- --force: help text now "Run now: no wait for the drawn moment, no window, no calendar (a manual run)." Implementation note: the drawn moment stays in WindowedRun and run(force=True) waits for nothing, ignores window/calendar, planned_at None. NOT moment = now.time(): window_from refuses a window crossing midnight, so a manual run at 23:55-24:00 would crash (pinned by test_a_forced_run_just_before_midnight_still_runs).
- --dry-run output: after "would run now: ..." a new line "would wait until: HH:MM" ONLY when the run would first wait for its moment; after "calendar: ..." a new line "schedule: today HH:MM / HH:MM" (check-in / check-out) always; the steps list now includes the loop's "wait until the drawn moment HH:MM if started from HH:MM; earlier is skipped as too early".
- probe output: settings line now "settings: ok - portal <url>, desktop '<desktop>', check-in <HT_CHECKIN_RANGE>, check-out <HT_CHECKOUT_RANGE>, <zone>" (ranges, was the HT-001 windows); a fifth line "schedule: today HH:MM / HH:MM" with NO status (literal per CONTEXT), from the same draw a run makes today. Other lines unchanged.

Environment the CLI reads now (via Settings.from_env): HORIZON_URL, HORIZON_USERNAME, HORIZON_PASSWORD, HORIZON_DESKTOP, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID, HT_TIMEZONE, HT_CHECKIN_RANGE (07:30-08:10), HT_CHECKOUT_RANGE (16:30-17:10), HT_SESSION_LENGTH_MINUTES (540), HT_SESSION_EXTRA_MAX_MINUTES (10), HT_WINDOW_GRACE_MINUTES (5), HT_JITTER_SEED (optional; unset/blank -> HORIZON_USERNAME in UTF-8; never printed), HT_HOLD_SECONDS, HT_CHROME_PATH, HT_ARTIFACTS_DIR. HT_CHECKIN_WINDOW / HT_CHECKOUT_WINDOW present (even blank) -> every command exits 1 "configuration error: HT_CHECKIN_WINDOW: ..." (BEAD-03 behaviour, now the only one). Timers must fire at the range starts (07:30 / 16:30) for the wait to happen: a timer later than the drawn moment + grace skips the run as window_missed.

Settings (horizon_tracker.infrastructure.config): REMOVED fields checkin_window, checkout_window and constants HT001_CHECKIN_WINDOW, HT001_CHECKOUT_WINDOW. No field holds a Window any more (pinned by test_no_window_is_a_setting_each_is_drawn_from_its_range).

horizon_tracker.domain.schedule (Window, RunKind, Decision, RetryPolicy, decide, FIRST_ATTEMPT unchanged):
- TimeRange(start: time, end: time) — frozen; both ends included; ValueError when start >= end ("range start .. must be before its end ..") or when either end has seconds/microseconds ("range ends must be whole minutes, got ..").
- DailyMoments(check_in: time, check_out: time) — frozen.
- draw_moments(day: date, seed: bytes, checkin_range: TimeRange, session_length: timedelta, extra_max: timedelta, checkout_range: TimeRange) -> DailyMoments
  digest = hmac.new(seed, day.isoformat().encode(), "sha256").digest(); check_in = checkin_range.start + minutes(int.from_bytes(digest[:4], "big") % (span_minutes + 1)); check_out = clip(check_in + session_length + minutes(int.from_bytes(digest[4:8], "big") % (extra_max_minutes + 1)), checkout_range). Whole minutes.
  ValueError for: empty seed ("the draw needs a non-empty seed"); session_length <= 0; extra_max < 0; session_length or extra_max not whole minutes; checkout_range.start <= checkin_range.end ("the check-out range must start after the check-in range ends: ..").
  BEAD-03: Settings should run the same checks at load (or construct the ranges and call draw_moments once on load) so a bad .env fails at start, not at 07:30. TimeRange itself refuses sub-minute ends.
- window_from(moment: time, grace: timedelta) -> Window — Window(moment, moment + grace); ValueError when grace <= 0 ("grace must be positive, got ..") or the window would cross midnight.
  BEAD-02/04: --force passes moment = now.time(); now.time() carries seconds, which window_from accepts (only TimeRange is minute-only).

- RunReport(kind, outcome, at, verdict_source, reason=None, screenshot=None, planned_at: time | None = None) — planned_at type-checked (TypeError "RunReport.planned_at has the wrong type: <type>").

title: [HT-002] Review: the adapter against the bundle, whether the new tests bite
description: Spec: BRIEF.md BEAD-02

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
REVIEW ISSUES: 0 critical, 1 major

Reviewed: 39b1149 + d69cf64 (HT-002 BEAD-01, bead ht-m7u) against BRIEF HT-002 and the real bundle app-htmlaccess.4eb7424a56fc03317f06.js (read by grep, never executed).

Where this was measured:
- Clean room room-ht-75w (beadloom clean-room), HEAD bf3e509, 0 carried files, CPython 3.13.16, extras dev, Linux x86_64, Playwright Chromium from /opt/pw-browsers. The VPS runs CPython 3.12 with the system Chrome; this run does not cover that environment.
- Baseline in the room: full suite 470 passed, 7 skipped (HT-003 placeholders, reason printed by -rs). Adapter file: 29 passed. ruff check clean, ruff format --check clean on both touched files, mypy src tests: 0 issues in 65 files.
- beadloom ci on the tree: rc 0 (reindex, lint 0 errors, sync-check 32 pairs fresh, doctor 0 errors). That gate does not run the suite.

Selectors checked against the bundle, all confirmed:
- Tile: the compiled template sw renders li#{id} > button#launch-{id}.ui-desktop-corner[title=name]. Inside that button: the icons, button.overflow-button.app-item-action[aria-haspopup=true], and share-contextmenu.content-menu while it is open. Then div.ellipsis > p.ui-desktop-name. So ANY_TILE, the tile-by-name selector, LAUNCH_BUTTON and TILE_MENU_BUTTON are correct. toggleContextMenu calls stopPropagation, so opening the menu never reaches launchDesktop.
- Menu: share-contextmenu > ul#context-menu-container.context-menu-container > web-contextmenu > li#menu-item-logoff-btn. The item uses the hidden property binding, which reflects to the attribute. showLogOffDesktop = isDesktop && !isShadow && (logoffEnabled || canLogoff===true || isRunning || _isRunningItem), and on the list logoffEnabled = canLogoff=="true" && state!="". dismissContentMenuFromOutside listens for a click on the document and has no keydown handler, so closing with a body click is correct.
- Canvas: _initWmksContainer appends div#wmksContainer<N> (display:none) with canvas#mainCanvas to en.CANVAS_PARENT_ID = "#canvas-container", and createPrimaryCanvas appends canvas#primary-monitor there. canvas#canvas in app-root is a hidden sibling, not a child. DESKTOP_CANVAS and _CANVAS_IS_DRAWN match this.
- The confirmation's #okDialogBtn exists in the client's confirm modal.

Sabotage in the room. Each was a single exact replacement, reversed byte-for-byte and asserted equal afterwards. The shared tree was never edited. Collected count every time: 29.
- S1, _offered changed to is_enabled(): 7 failed, including test_log_off_without_a_session_is_already_logged_off and test_a_checkout_of_a_desktop_without_a_session_reads_it_and_is_already_logged_off.
- S2, menu closed with Escape: 9 failed, including test_log_off_after_reading_the_state_ends_the_session.
- S3, DESKTOP_CANVAS set back to "#canvas-container #canvas": 3 failed: test_open_desktop_cancels_fullscreen_and_returns_once_blast_is_up, test_the_blast_socket_path_does_not_decide_whether_the_desktop_opened, test_disconnect_lets_go_and_leaves_the_windows_session_running.
- S4, ANY_TILE set back to "li[title]": 17 failed.
- S5, _css_string without escaping: 1 failed, test_a_tile_is_found_by_a_name_with_quotes_and_a_backslash.
- S6, Blast socket required for the "open" verdict again: 1 failed, test_the_blast_socket_path_does_not_decide_whether_the_desktop_opened.
- S7, the wait_for(state="hidden") line in _close_tile_menu removed: 0 failed, 29 passed. See Minor 1.
- S8, the fixture changed to model what the bundle does on the log-off confirmation (the adapter left untouched): 1 failed, test_a_log_off_the_portal_never_confirms_fails_with_a_screenshot. See Major 1.

Major:
1. src/horizon_tracker/infrastructure/horizon_playwright.py:212-217 (log_off confirmation), with tests/fixtures/htmlaccess/app-htmlaccess.fixture.js:118-129 and 174-177. Severity: Major.
   Issue: the bundle's confirm callback in launchItemsCtrlService._logoffDesktop is
     t=e=>{e.logoffEnabled=!1,this.jscdkCommonInvoker.logoffDesktop(e.id),...}
   It clears the tile's flag synchronously, before the kill-session request leaves for the broker through the router worker, and long before the broker answers. The menu derives showLogOffDesktop from that flag. Because log_off polls _tile_session_state on the same page, its first poll reads NO_SESSION from the client's own optimistic state. Two consequences:
   - On the real client, LOGOFF_NOT_CONFIRMED cannot be reached after a successful OK click.
   - EveningCheckout's second desktop_status reads the same flag, so a log off the broker refused or never received is reported as SUCCEEDED with exit 0.
   The fixture keeps this from showing. Its menu asks /fixture/launch-items every time it opens, which the fixture header itself calls "the fixture's own". So test_a_log_off_the_portal_never_confirms_fails_with_a_screenshot is green only because the fake differs from the client in exactly the property the test asserts. S8 changes the fixture to set a cleared flag on OK and read it in the menu, and that test goes red against the unchanged adapter.
   The SPEC (lines 87-89) names the optimistic flag and leaves it to the live checkout --force. A successful live log off looks the same whether the confirmation came from the broker or from the flag, so that measurement cannot answer the question it is given.
   Recommendation:
   (a) Make the confirmation read broker state. Before each confirmation read, rebuild the tile from a fresh list: a new login in a fresh context (the adapter already does this when no page is live), or a reload of #/launchitems if a live run shows it keeps the session. Waiting for the kill-session response is a weaker option.
   (b) Make the fixture model the bundle: clear the session flag on OK, and restore broker state only when the list is fetched again. The existing ignore_logoff test then pins (a).
   (c) Add a check to BEAD-03 (ht-28a) that can tell the two apart, for example a broker-side read after checkout, or the timing of the first NO_SESSION read relative to the kill-session response.

Minor:
1. horizon_playwright.py:362. The wait_for(state="hidden") in _close_tile_menu is not pinned by any test: S7 removes it and all 29 tests pass. The fixture removes the menu synchronously inside the click handler, so the wait never waits. Recommendation: have the fixture defer closing the menu (setTimeout) and add an assertion that observes the menu closing, or accept the gap and say so in the SPEC Testing section.
2. .claude/development/docs/features/HT-001/RFC.md:132,135 and PLAN.md:186 still give li[title="DEV desktop"], "#canvas in #canvas-container" and a Blast WebSocket that gates the verdict, with no note that HT-002 superseded them. These are TO-BE documents of a closed epic, so they are not AS-IS drift. A future reader will still find wrong selectors there. Recommendation: add a one-line note under the RFC table: "superseded by HT-002, see SPEC horizon-playwright-client".

Nitpick:
- BRIEF HT-002, Problem item 1, describes the overflow button as a sibling of button#launch-<id>. In the bundle it is nested inside it. The code comment (horizon_playwright.py:64-65) and SPEC line 60 are correct; the BRIEF is not.
- horizon_playwright.py:304-305: the _tile_session_state docstring wraps early ("The tile" alone on its line).

Checked with no finding: layering (the adapter imports domain only, and the "# beadloom:domain=infrastructure" annotation is unchanged), typing, error handling (_step still drops the Playwright cause), secrets (no change on the password or screenshot paths), SPEC freshness (selector table and API list include TILE_MENU), cohesion of the two new module helpers.

Independence: the launch prompt carried no author summary. However, I read ACTIVE.md HT-002 as a work-item document before the bundle, and its Results row carries the author's account, including the risk that the client marks the desktop logged off before the broker answers. Major 1 was derived independently from the bundle and confirmed by S8, but I was primed toward it, and the review-brief withholding was partly defeated by ACTIVE.md.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
REVIEW FINDINGS: amendment after --release. The verdict stays at 0 critical, 1 major.

- The author's deviation 3 (Escape replaced by a document click) is correct. dismissContentMenuFromOutside only listens for a document click, and toggleContextMenu toggles the menu. S2 in this review confirms test_log_off_after_reading_the_state_ends_the_session pins it.
- Major 1 matches the author's "risk 4", which was deferred to BEAD-03 with a stated reason. The severity stays Major for three reasons:
  (i) Per the bundle, LOGOFF_NOT_CONFIRMED is unreachable after the OK click, and the one test of that path is green only because the fixture differs from the client exactly there (S8).
  (ii) The Mac check in BEAD-03 judges one live log off that succeeded. It cannot show where the adapter's NO_SESSION reading came from, and it does not protect later timer runs, in which a log off the broker refused would be reported SUCCEEDED with exit 0.
  (iii) A fix is available without a live login: rebuild the tile from a fresh broker list before each confirmation read, and make the fixture model the optimistic flag.
  If the owner accepts the risk as is, the fixture's ignore_logoff test should at least be renamed or marked as testing the fixture's contract, not the client's.
- Identity: --release reports that this verdict and the bead's author share the tracker identity Claude. The review was run by a separate reviewer subagent that never read ht-m7u's comments before the verdict above was recorded. The tracker cannot prove that.
- Measurement difference: the author ran on the tree before bf3e509 (beadloom ci rc 1, 14 HT-003 scenario-coverage errors). This review ran in a clean room on bf3e509, where the suite was 470 passed, 7 skipped, and beadloom ci on the tree returned rc 0.

The review bead is closed at the coordinator's instruction. Major 1 needs a fix bead before BEAD-03 (ht-28a) and the timers.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
REVIEW PASSED: 0 critical, 0 major, 2 minor, 1 nitpick. All six findings of ht-9uk are answered, and nothing regressed.

Scope: the HT-001 range main...0811cf7, with the fix commit 8fd731f (bead ht-jz5.2) read line by line against the ht-9uk verdict.
Withholding: defeated before the run. The launch prompt named the author's two departures (the probe split into client_bundles() and browser_version(); FIRST_ATTEMPT in domain/schedule.py) and the fix list. The coordinator also allowed reading ht-9uk, and I read it first. I did not read the ht-jz5.2 comments before this verdict.

Environment. pytest, coverage, ruff, mypy, mutmut and lint ran in the clean room room-ht-jz5.3 (HEAD 0811cf7, no carried files, extras "dev", CPython 3.13.16, Linux x86_64). CI runs CPython 3.12, and this room did not enter it. lint --strict and doctor ran on an index the room built from nothing. sync-check and diff ran on the tree. The tree was clean and equal to HEAD.

== Measurements ==
- The CI line "pytest -q -rs --cov --cov-report=term-missing": 466 passed (441 unit and acceptance, 25 Playwright on the fixture; that was 421/21 at ht-9uk). Coverage is 98.47 % against the floor of 80 %, and horizon_playwright is at 95 % (87 % before).
- The floor bites. With fail_under raised to 99 in the room, the same line printed "FAIL Required test coverage of 99.0% not reached. Total coverage: 98.47%" and exited 1. Reverted, and the file is identical to HEAD.
- ruff check: clean. ruff format --check: 64 files already formatted. mypy --strict: clean on src (20 files) and on src plus tests (64 files).
- mutmut over domain/: 111 mutants, 111 killed, 0 survived, 0 skipped. The count is unchanged, and __pycache__ was cleaned afterwards.
- Fresh index in the room: lint --strict exit 0, doctor exit 0. beadloom diff --since main shows the same 5 nodes and 8 edges as at ht-9uk, with no new edge.
- Secrets: the fix commits add no credential. The only token-shaped string in the tree is the fake in tests/unit/infrastructure/test_telegram.py:19.

== Findings of ht-9uk, one by one ==
- Major (no coverage gate): ANSWERED. ci.yml runs pytest with --cov. Three cases in test_ci_workflow pin the flag, the floor value and the concurrency setting. Sabotage S1 (drop --cov) turns test_ci_measures_coverage_so_the_floor_can_fail_the_run red.
- Minor 1 (vacuous PNG byte search): ANSWERED. The test now asserts the asked routes and the exact set of written files. Sabotage S6 (LOGIN_ROUTE photographed) now turns BOTH test_a_rejected_login_takes_no_screenshot_of_the_login_page and test_the_password_never_leaves_the_adapter red. At ht-9uk only the first one turned red.
- Minor 2 (greenlet concurrency): ANSWERED, measured 87 % -> 95 %.
- Minor 3 (the probe never started Chrome): ANSWERED in code. browser_version() launches headless Chrome at chrome_path, reads the version, closes the browser, and opens no page. S4 (no close) and S8 (opens a page) each turn red test_the_browser_version_is_read_from_a_started_chrome_that_opens_no_page. S5 (the probe skips the launch) turns 5 tests red, including the BDD probe scenario. The residual is Minor 1 below.
- Minor 4 (DryRun duplicating the loop): ANSWERED. DryRun takes the use case and reads WindowedRun.first_decision() and the steps() of each use case. S7 (first_decision ignores force) turns 4 tests red, including test_forced_dry_run_names_the_force_and_asks_no_calendar.
- Minor 5 (prune and teardown): ANSWERED. S2 (prune no longer catches OSError) turns test_an_artifact_directory_that_cannot_be_pruned_does_not_stop_the_run[checkin/checkout] red. S3 (_close_quietly re-raises) turns test_a_teardown_error_is_logged_by_type_and_never_raised[Browser/BrowserContext] red.
- Minor 6: it is a CONTEXT row (2026-10-20, the window bounds the START of an attempt). That is an acceptable decision with a stated reason.
Every sabotage was a precise text edit in the room, reverted by the reverse edit and diffed against HEAD (identical). Every baseline was counted (441 and 25 passed) before the sabotage, and every red result above is a named FAILED.

== The author's departures ==
- The probe split into client_bundles() and browser_version(): SOUND. Each port method answers one question. Probe._chrome tries the launch only after the file is found, and test_a_missing_chrome_fails_the_probe_without_starting_anything checks that order. The client and the Probe take chrome_path from the same Settings field (cli.py:112, :228). One cost: a port in the domain now names a browser. That is acceptable because the RFC chose the web client, and no domain module imports a browser.
- FIRST_ATTEMPT public in domain/schedule.py: SOUND. It is defined exactly once (grep), and application -> domain is the allowed direction.

== Minor ==
1. tests/acceptance/features/checks_without_login.feature:11, PRD.md:112 and :142, RFC.md:108, PLAN.md:114/189/208. Issue: the scenario is still titled "Probe reports the portal version without logging in", but its Thens now assert client bundles and a Chrome version. The PRD, RFC and PLAN also say "portal version" / probe(). The contract was renamed in code and not in the approved documents. The scenario title is the verbatim link to the PRD catalogue, so the name cannot change in one place only. Recommendation: amend the PRD scenario name, for example "Probe names the client bundles and the Chrome version without logging in", together with the .feature title, in ht-6rw. This is a PRD amendment, not a mechanical refresh.
2. deploy/RUNBOOK.md:175 (§3, the chrome row). Issue: the normal line is now "ok - Chrome <version> started from <path>", and there is a new failure, "failed - found at <path> but did not start: unexpected", which needs an operator remedy: Chrome updated past what the pinned Playwright drives, or missing libraries. RUNBOOK is not a sync-check pair, so no gate will flag it. Recommendation: add the row and the remedy in ht-6rw.

== Nitpick ==
- tests/integration/infrastructure/test_horizon_playwright.py, record_close(browser: Browser, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any): Any with no stated reason. object would do, as in refuse() just above it.
- in_seconds() is a formatting helper in windowed_run.py that checkin.py imports. It is acceptable while the step lists are its only users.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
API CHANGE (application public API for BEAD-07 CLI; deviations from PLAN BEAD-03):

1. A third module, application/windowed_run.py: WindowedRun(calendar, clock, notifier, window: Window, policy: RetryPolicy), frozen; run(kind: RunKind, attempt: Callable[[], AttemptResult], *, force=False) -> RunReport. AttemptResult(outcome: Outcome, at: datetime, reason: Reason | None = None, screenshot: Path | None = None). Why: the verdict -> decide -> retry -> one-report loop is identical for both use cases (~60 lines); writing it twice would duplicate the rule that holds "exactly one notification per run". Scope deviation: the coordinator named only checkin.py/checkout.py; the new file is inside this bead's own package, which no other wave-2 bead touches.
2. Constructors are not PLAN's MorningCheckin(client, calendar, notifier, clock, artifacts, settings). They are MorningCheckin(client, clock, runner: WindowedRun, desktop: str, hold: timedelta) and EveningCheckout(client, clock, runner: WindowedRun, desktop: str); both .run(*, force=False) -> RunReport. The CLI builds one WindowedRun per kind (checkin window vs checkout window, same calendar/clock/notifier/policy). No Settings: application must not import infrastructure.config, so the CLI unpacks Settings into these values.
3. No ArtifactStore argument: HorizonClient has no screenshot method, the adapter puts the screenshot into HorizonClientError, so the use case had nothing to ask the store. The CLI hands the store to the adapter (as PLAN BEAD-06 already does).
4. application/__init__ re-exports MorningCheckin, EveningCheckout, WindowedRun, AttemptResult.

Contract the use cases rely on from HorizonClient (for BEAD-06 ht-xlh / BEAD-13 probe): (a) desktop_status(name) must work while the desktop is open on #/desktop (RFC: broker XML from the authenticated context; the tile is not on that page); (b) login() is called again after disconnect() closed the browser context, and again on every retry after a failure; (c) checkin calls disconnect() in a finally once open_desktop returned, so it may follow a failed desktop_status.

Mapping decided here: SKIP_NON_WORKING_DAY -> SKIPPED/NON_WORKING_DAY; SKIP_LATE and SKIP_EARLY -> SKIPPED/WINDOW_MISSED (only when no attempt was made); GIVE_UP, or a window that closes between retries, -> FAILED with the LAST failure's reason and screenshot. Unconfirmed check-in -> DESKTOP_DID_NOT_OPEN; unconfirmed log off -> LOGOFF_NOT_CONFIRMED; no session at the first look -> SKIPPED/ALREADY_LOGGED_OFF, not retried. Any exception other than HorizonClientError from an attempt is a failed attempt with Reason.UNEXPECTED (retried); its message is never logged (type + traceback frames only), because adapter text may quote what it typed. Report time: check-in success = the moment open_desktop returned (before the hold); check-out success = the moment the log off was confirmed; skips/failures = when the run ended.

Known gap (domain, not fixed here): Reason has no member for "started before the window", so SKIP_EARLY renders as "the run started after its window", which is false for an early start. Needs a domain Reason (e.g. WINDOW_NOT_OPEN) and its _REASON_TEXT; owner: coordinator.

Docs to check: docs/domains/application/README.md (sync-check: missing modules checkin, checkout, windowed_run), PLAN.md BEAD-03 and BEAD-07 signatures, RFC.md application table (add windowed_run).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
API CHANGE: new public domain API for BEAD-03 (application) to consume.
- horizon_tracker.domain.calendar: VerdictSource (StrEnum: CALENDAR, WEEKDAY_FALLBACK); WorkingDayVerdict(is_working: bool, source: VerdictSource), frozen; weekday_rule(day: date) -> bool; resolve(calendar_answer: bool | None, day: date) -> WorkingDayVerdict.
- horizon_tracker.domain.schedule: RunKind (StrEnum: CHECKIN="checkin", CHECKOUT="checkout"); Decision (StrEnum: RUN, RETRY, SKIP_EARLY, SKIP_LATE, SKIP_NON_WORKING_DAY, GIVE_UP); Window(start: time, end: time), frozen, start < end enforced, contains(moment) with BOTH ends inclusive; RetryPolicy(max_attempts: int >= 1, backoff: timedelta >= 0), frozen; decide(now: datetime, window, verdict, attempt: int (from 1), policy) -> Decision.
DEVIATION FROM PLAN (two extra Decision members): PLAN listed RUN/RETRY/SKIP_LATE/SKIP_NON_WORKING_DAY. decide() takes attempt+policy, so it needs an outcome for spent attempts -> GIVE_UP; and a start before the window (07:54:59) must not run and is not 'late' -> SKIP_EARLY. BEAD-03 must handle both (GIVE_UP = failure report 'all attempts failed'; SKIP_EARLY = skip report).
Precedence in decide(): attempt<1 -> ValueError; non-working day -> SKIP_NON_WORKING_DAY (even outside the window, so the notice says 'holiday', not 'late'); attempt > max_attempts -> GIVE_UP (even after the window closed); before start -> SKIP_EARLY; after end -> SKIP_LATE; attempt 1 -> RUN; else RETRY.
backoff is a timedelta; the use case passes backoff.total_seconds() to Clock.sleep. now is read as wall time (now.time()), i.e. in the zone the Clock hands out (Europe/Moscow); tzinfo is not converted.
Docs to check: docs/domains/domain/README.md (does NOT name the calendar module -> Gate red, see COMPLETED), RFC.md domain table (decide signature now carries attempt+policy; Decision has 6 members).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
API CHANGE (new domain API; two deliberate deviations from PLAN BEAD-02 for BEAD-03..06 to read):
1. session.checkin_succeeded(while_open, after_disconnect) -- PLAN said (before, after). A `before` has no say in check-in success (fresh logon, reconnect and takeover all end the same), so an unused param would have been a lie. The rule is the transition CONNECTED -> DISCONNECTED: Blast was open (logon done), then the client let go without logging off. checkout_succeeded(before, after) as planned: before.has_session and after is NO_SESSION; NO_SESSION->NO_SESSION is NOT success (BEAD-03 reports it as Outcome.SKIPPED + Reason.ALREADY_LOGGED_OFF). SessionState is a StrEnum with a `has_session` property; DesktopStatus(name, state) frozen.
2. Notifier.send(report) -- PLAN said send(report, screenshot=None). RunReport already carries `screenshot`; a second argument would be a second source of truth. The notifier attaches report.screenshot when present.
Other shapes: RunReport(kind: RunKind, outcome: Outcome, at: aware datetime, verdict_source: VerdictSource | None [None = --force, calendar not asked], reason: Reason | None, screenshot: Path | None). `reason` is a closed vocabulary (Reason enum), not free text -- that is what makes "render never contains the password" true by construction; the PLAN wording "reason" as text could not satisfy the password test. Invariants enforced at construction: runtime type checks on every field (TypeError, message never echoes the value), aware `at` (ValueError), reason present iff outcome is not SUCCEEDED (ValueError). render() text is Russian at this point (in the catalogue's English rendering: headline "Check-in succeeded"/"Check-out failed"/..., "Time: dd.mm.yyyy HH:MM:SS MSK", "Calendar: ...", "Reason: ..."); the screenshot is never in the text.
ports.HorizonClientError(reason: Reason, screenshot: Path | None = None); str(error) == reason.value. Adapters (BEAD-06) raise it; use cases (BEAD-03) catch it by name. HorizonClient.login() takes no credentials -- the adapter is constructed with them. probe() -> str (portal version), unreachable = HorizonClientError(PORTAL_UNREACHABLE). Clock.now() returns an aware datetime in the service tz. ArtifactStore.screenshot_path(kind: RunKind) -> Path.
Reason vocabulary: NON_WORKING_DAY, WINDOW_MISSED, ALREADY_LOGGED_OFF, PORTAL_UNREACHABLE, LOGIN_REJECTED, DESKTOP_NOT_FOUND, DESKTOP_DID_NOT_OPEN, LOGOFF_NOT_CONFIRMED, UNEXPECTED. Extending it is a domain change (render maps every member; a test fails if one renders empty or duplicates another).
Docs to check: docs/domains/domain/README.md (Responsibilities lists no report module; sync-check flags it stale -- see COMPLETED), PLAN.md BEAD-02/03 signatures, RFC domain table (report "reason" is a closed vocabulary).

1. .github/workflows/ci.yml:62 and pyproject.toml:57-60. Severity: Major.
   Issue: the coverage floor is declared but no gate evaluates it. [tool.coverage.report]
   fail_under = 80 takes effect only when pytest runs with --cov. CI runs
   `uv run pytest -q -rs`, addopts has no --cov, and beadloom ci does not run the suite.
   PLAN BEAD-10 asks for "Coverage >= 80 % over src/, a report in CI". Today the floor is met
   (96.4 %) only because someone ran it by hand. The day it drops, nothing goes red. This
   is the class the project layer warns about: a gate that reads as present and checks
   nothing.
   Recommendation: make the CI step `uv run pytest -q -rs --cov --cov-report=term-missing`,
   so that fail_under fails the run. Pin it with a case in
   tests/unit/deploy/test_ci_workflow.py (the pytest step carries --cov). Add Minor 2's
   concurrency setting in the same change, so that the reported figure is true.

== Minor ==
1. tests/integration/infrastructure/test_horizon_playwright.py, in
   test_the_password_never_leaves_the_adapter. Issue: the assertion
   `PASSWORD.encode() not in path.read_bytes()` over the screenshot files cannot fail. A PNG
   holds compressed pixels, never the typed text, and a password field renders as dots
   anyway. Sabotage 6 photographs the login page and this test stays green. The real guard
   is test_a_rejected_login_takes_no_screenshot_of_the_login_page, and it bites.
   Recommendation: replace the byte search with an assertion on which routes the adapter
   asked the artifact store to photograph, as the allowlist test does. Or drop it and let
   the allowlist test carry the claim, so that this test does not report a protection it
   does not measure.
2. pyproject.toml [tool.coverage.run]. Issue: there is no `concurrency`, and Playwright's
   sync API runs on greenlets, so the lines it executes are under-counted. horizon_playwright
   reads 87 % with lines 160-162 and 221-233 "missed". With `concurrency = ["greenlet",
   "thread"]` the same 21 tests measure 94 %, and those lines are covered. Recommendation:
   add the setting.
3. application/probe.py Probe._chrome, infrastructure/horizon_playwright.py probe(), and
   the RFC Risks row "Chrome on the VPS updated and broke Playwright -> probe in the deploy as a
   smoke". Issue: the probe only checks Path.is_file on the binary and reads index.html
   through Playwright's request context. It never launches Chrome, so the deploy smoke
   cannot catch the risk the RFC assigns to it. Separately, the port docstring and the PRD
   scenario say "portal version", but the adapter returns bundle file names
   (app-htmlaccess.<hash>.js), and the BDD scenario passes on the fake's "fake-2312".
   Recommendation: have the probe launch headless Chrome at chrome_path, read
   browser.version and close it, with no navigation. Alternatively, correct the RFC
   mitigation. Then either read a real version or rename the contract to "client bundles".
4. application/probe.py DryRun.plan, _checkin_steps and _checkout_steps. Issue: DryRun
   re-implements WindowedRun's first decision (forced RUN with source None, otherwise
   resolve + decide), and it hand-writes the steps that MorningCheckin and EveningCheckout
   perform. These are two copies that can drift silently: the dry run would then describe a
   run that no longer exists. Recommendation: expose WindowedRun's first decision as a
   method that DryRun calls, and keep each use case's step list beside the use case.
   _FIRST_ATTEMPT is also defined three times (schedule, probe, windowed_run).
5. cli.py:186 (`adapters.artifacts.prune()`) and the adapter teardown in open_adapters.
   Issue: the "one report per run" invariant holds only inside WindowedRun. An OSError from
   prune aborts the run before any attempt, sends no Telegram message, and prints a
   traceback. A PlaywrightError from browser.close() after a SUCCEEDED report exits 1, so
   systemd marks a successful run failed. Recommendation: make prune best-effort (catch
   OSError and log the type), and make close() log and swallow a PlaywrightError.
6. application/windowed_run.py and domain/schedule.py, against the PRD goal "a tolerance of at
   most 5 minutes". Issue: the window bounds when an attempt STARTS, not when the logon
   happens. A retry started at 07:59:50 can open the desktop at about 08:01:30 (login 30 s
   plus open 90 s). Recommendation: either document that the window bounds the start
   (CONTEXT row), or end the retry window early by the worst-case attempt duration.
7. application/checkin.py:41. This is a hypothesis to measure in BEAD-13, not a proven
   defect. The 120 s hold is Clock.sleep, which is time.sleep, and it does not pump
   Playwright's sync event loop. Playwright's guidance is page.wait_for_timeout for that
   reason. Recommendation: on the first VPS run, confirm that the Blast WebSocket is still
   reported open after the hold. If it is not, let the adapter hold the page (for example
   with a HorizonClient.hold(seconds)).

== Nitpick ==
- ConfigError and HorizonClientError have no common project base exception.
- morning_checkin.feature "reports success with the recorded time": the Given "held open
  for 120 seconds" has no observable consequence in its Thens.

Not closed: a Major requires a fix cycle (review role protocol).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
API CHANGE (public interface = the horizon CLI + the environment; for the deploy bead ht-2h2, the workflows bead ht-spa and the docs bead ht-6rw). Commit f0f958c.

COMMANDS
- horizon --version            -> "horizon, version 0.1.0", exit 0
- horizon --help               -> lists exactly: checkin, checkout, probe
- horizon checkin  [--dry-run] [--force]
- horizon checkout [--dry-run] [--force]
- horizon probe
--force   : ignore the window and the calendar (manual run from the VPS); the report then says the calendar was not asked.
--dry-run : print the plan to stdout and exit 0; never calls login or any other Horizon method, sends no Telegram report, prunes nothing. The calendar IS asked (read-only GET to isdayoff.ru) unless --force is also given. Both flags combine.

EXIT CODES
- checkin/checkout: 1 iff the run's report is Outcome.FAILED; 0 for SUCCEEDED and for every deliberate skip (non-working day, before/after the window, already logged off). systemd marks the unit failed exactly on a failed run.
- checkin/checkout --dry-run: 0.
- probe: 1 if any check FAILED (portal unreachable / no bundles, Chrome binary missing); 0 otherwise. An unreachable isdayoff.ru is DEGRADED (runs fall back to Mon-Fri) and does NOT fail the probe -> a deploy smoke `horizon probe` is not broken by an isdayoff outage.
- every command: 1 on a configuration error, logged on stderr as "configuration error: <VAR>: <problem>" (no traceback, no value of a credential). A Telegram token that TelegramNotifier refuses (e.g. a trailing newline from .env) is reported as "configuration error: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN: ..." before anything runs; nothing is stripped silently.

OUTPUT
- stdout: only the dry-run plan and the probe lines. Probe lines, in order: "settings: ok - portal <HORIZON_URL>, desktop '<HORIZON_DESKTOP>', check-in HH:MM-HH:MM, check-out HH:MM-HH:MM, <tz>", "portal: ok|failed - <HTML Access bundles: ...|no answer: <reason>>", "calendar: ok|degraded - ...", "chrome: ok|failed - found at|not found at <HT_CHROME_PATH>".
- stderr: logging, level INFO, format "%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s", handler on the "horizon_tracker" package logger (not root). The journal of a systemd unit captures it; there is no log file (PLAN said "stderr and file": the file is left to journald, so no rotation code).

ENVIRONMENT READ (Settings.from_env(os.environ), unchanged from ht-c5q)
Required: HORIZON_URL, HORIZON_USERNAME, HORIZON_PASSWORD, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID.
Optional (default): HORIZON_DESKTOP ("DEV desktop"), HT_TIMEZONE (Europe/Moscow), HT_CHECKIN_WINDOW (07:55-08:00), HT_CHECKOUT_WINDOW (17:00-17:05), HT_HOLD_SECONDS (120), HT_CHROME_PATH (/usr/bin/google-chrome), HT_ARTIFACTS_DIR (/opt/horizon-tracker/artifacts).
Not configurable: retry policy cli.RETRY_POLICY = 3 attempts, 30 s apart (the window still ends a scheduled run; under --force the count is the bound).

PYTHON SURFACE
- horizon_tracker.application.probe: CheckStatus(OK, DEGRADED, FAILED), Check(name, status, detail), ProbeReport(checks).ok, Probe(client, calendar, clock, chrome_path, file_exists).run() -> ProbeReport; RunPlan(kind, at, forced, decision, verdict_source, steps).would_run, DryRun(calendar, clock, window, policy, desktop, hold).plan(kind, *, force=False) -> RunPlan. Not re-exported from application/__init__ (that file was outside this bead's scope).
- horizon_tracker.cli: Adapters(clock, calendar, notifier, horizon, artifacts), AdapterFactory = Callable[[Settings, RunKind], ContextManager[Adapters]], open_adapters (the production factory), RETRY_POLICY, EXIT_OK/EXIT_FAILED. Tests inject a factory via CliRunner().invoke(main, args, obj=factory).

Docs to check: docs/services/cli.md (commands table lists only --version; sync-check stale), docs/domains/application/README.md (missing module: probe; sync-check stale), RFC "API Changes" (required vs defaulted), deploy/RUNBOOK.md (first live run: `horizon probe`, then `horizon checkin --dry-run --force`, then `horizon checkin --force`).

The room built no interpreter of its own: the verdict was taken under /home/user/horizon-tracker/.venv/bin/python with PYTHONPATH=<room>/src:<room>. comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
API CHANGE (for BEAD-07 ht-oqx, the CLI composition root): horizon_tracker.infrastructure.horizon_playwright

PlaywrightHorizonClient(*, horizon_url: str, username: str, password: str, chrome_path: Path | None, artifacts: ArtifactStore, run_kind: RunKind, timeouts: HorizonTimeouts | None = None)
- Differs from PLAN "PlaywrightHorizonClient(settings, artifacts)". The ctor is keyword-only and does not import infrastructure.config.Settings: that module was still being written in parallel (ht-c5q). The CLI wires it as horizon_url=settings.horizon_url, username=settings.username, password=settings.password, chrome_path=settings.chrome_path, artifacts=<ArtifactStore>, run_kind=RunKind.CHECKIN|CHECKOUT.
- run_kind is new: ArtifactStore.screenshot_path(kind) needs it, and the port methods do not carry it.
- chrome_path=None means Playwright's own bundled Chromium (useful in CI); the VPS passes HT_CHROME_PATH.
- HorizonTimeouts(page_load_ms=30000, action_ms=15000, login_ms=30000, desktop_open_ms=90000, logoff_confirm_ms=60000, poll_ms=1000): frozen dataclass, defaults sized for the live portal.
- Context manager, plus close(). Use `with PlaywrightHorizonClient(...) as client:`. The sync Playwright driver refuses a second instance in the same thread, so close one client before building the next (the CLI's checkin and probe must not overlap in one process).
- probe() -> "HTML Access bundles: <name>, ..." (the <script src> basenames of index.html; no login, no browser launched). Raises PORTAL_UNREACHABLE on a network failure or non-200, and UNEXPECTED when the page names no bundle.
- desktop_status(name): CONNECTED only while this client holds that desktop open. Otherwise it reads the tile: an enabled #menu-item-logoff-btn means DISCONNECTED, a disabled one NO_SESSION. A client that has disconnected logs in again to read it, so checkin can read after_disconnect directly after disconnect().
- log_off(name) on a tile without a session raises ALREADY_LOGGED_OFF, and on an unconfirmed log off LOGOFF_NOT_CONFIRMED (after polling the tile).
- Reason mapping: goto/network -> PORTAL_UNREACHABLE; error dialog -> LOGIN_REJECTED; no verdict within login_ms -> UNEXPECTED; no tile -> DESKTOP_NOT_FOUND; signal not reached -> DESKTOP_DID_NOT_OPEN.
Docs to check: docs/domains/infrastructure/README.md (lists no horizon_playwright module; sync-check flags it stale), PLAN.md BEAD-06/07 ctor signature, RFC infrastructure table.

Biting: 15 sabotages by targeted reverse edit with a hash check after each restore, run against the named tests (red by name, not by colour):
- the signal ignores the websocket -> test_a_desktop_whose_blast_never_connects_did_not_open
- the signal ignores the canvas -> test_a_desktop_never_drawn_did_not_open

Two guards were vacuous on the first pass and were fixed rather than counted. The `from None` assertion sat on errors that never pass through _step, so it moved to the unreachable-portal test, which does. The #password mask on screenshots stayed green under sabotage because the route allowlist already excludes the login page and a password input renders as bullets, so I removed it as untestable rather than claiming it. Message redaction was removed for the same reason: errors are now logged by type only.

Findings:
1. beadloom binds tests only under tests/unit|integration, so tests/adapters/test_horizon_playwright.py is the "1 of 15 unplaced" test file. The infrastructure node counts 51 tests in 5 files and none of mine. CONTEXT puts adapter tests in tests/adapters/, while ht-c5q and ht-axc put theirs in tests/unit/infrastructure/. The coordinator or BEAD-12 should pick one.
2. Hypotheses until the first `horizon probe` on the VPS (BEAD-13), each isolated in one method whose docstring says so: _desktop_is_open (canvas non-zero AND a WS open on /r/ or /d/) and _tile_session_state (an enabled #menu-item-logoff-btn means a session exists; the tile cannot show another client attached). comments.text:
REVIEW ISSUES: 0 critical, 1 major

Room: the shared tree at ceaee33 on macOS arm64, not a clean room. Rooms not entered: every

Withholding: the launch prompt carried environment facts from the coordinator (the
pre-existing failures, a private repository, no tag yet). It carried no summary of the
change. I then defeated part of the withholding myself: a `git grep` over the diff reached
.beads/issues.jsonl and showed me ht-qdg's CHECKPOINT/API CHANGE/COMPLETED comments before

46-50, releasing.md, and a scratch measurement. Nothing below was changed by that reading.

Verified, no finding:
- Trigger matrix, as BRIEF states it. A PR or Dependabot PR starts ci.yml only. A push to
  main starts ci.yml once (branches-only filter, so no tag push). A tag v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+
  starts release.yml only. mutation.yml is schedule + dispatch. deploy.yml is removed.
- The deploy job moved faithfully. A YAML diff of deploy.yml@main against release.yml shows
  the same 10 steps in the same order. The only changes: DEPLOY_SHA comes from
  needs.verify.outputs.sha, the summary names the tag and version, and the
  `if: github.ref == refs/heads/main` guard is gone (see Minor-3).
- Secrets appear only in the deploy job's step env:. No ${{ }} inside a run script, no
  continue-on-error, no `|| true`, no set -x. The hygiene tests read all three files.
- Pages: writes happen only in portal-deploy (pages: write, id-token: write, the
  github-pages environment, concurrency group pages). portal-build has contents and pages
  read, as configure-pages needs. publish alone has contents: write.
- Pins: I checked the 6 new pins with git ls-remote against their upstream tags.
  download-artifact v8.0.2, deploy-pages v4.0.5, upload-pages-artifact v3.0.1,
  configure-pages v5.0.0, setup-node v5.0.0 and setup-python v6.3.0 all match.
- The portal jobs match what beadloom 9.0.0 writes. I generated
  `docs site --pages-workflow` in a scratch copy, outside the repository. The only
  differences are the two stated departures, plus the absent default-branch `if:`.
  PORTAL_BASE equals site.base, and a test holds the two equal.
- verify refuses a bad name, a missing tag, a tag off main, a pyproject mismatch and the
  CHANGELOG defects. The tests run its scripts in a temporary git repository. Every file is
  read through `git show $SHA:`, so a dispatch checks the tag and not main's head.
- The version has one source. __init__ reads importlib.metadata. test_cli holds
  `horizon --version` equal to the pyproject value. uv.lock and the Current version line
  read 1.0.0.
- ci.yml's workflow_call `ref` input feeds every checkout. Its concurrency group carries the
  caller's workflow name, so it never collides with release-horizon-vps.
  mutation-per-change is outside ci-ok.

Major:
1. .github/workflows/release.yml verify (lines 141-155) and ci.yml (every `uv sync --extra
   dev`) · Major.
   Issue: a release that bumps pyproject.toml without running `uv lock` passes verify and
   passes gate. CI's `uv sync` re-resolves and never checks the lock. The run then fails in
   deploy's "Update the code" step, AFTER `git checkout --detach` has moved the host to the
   tag's commit. The install is editable, so the timers then run the new code over the old
   environment. The v* ruleset forbids moving or deleting the tag, so that version number
   is lost. I measured this in a scratch copy: pyproject 1.0.0 -> 1.0.1 without `uv lock`.
   Both `uv lock --check` and `uv sync --locked` then refuse with "The lockfile at uv.lock
   needs to be updated". Every release now requires a bump, so this is the most likely
   release mistake. releasing.md step 2 documents the hazard ("a stale uv.lock passes CI
   and stops the deploy") instead of closing it.
   Recommendation: make CI refuse a stale lock at PR time. Use `uv sync --locked --extra
   dev` in the lint/types/tests/mutation jobs, or add one `uv lock --check` step to stage 1.
   Also add a verify step that refuses the tag when the uv.lock entry for horizon-tracker
   at $SHA is not $VERSION, named `verify: lock`. Then a tag that verify passes cannot
   stop the deploy halfway. Update releasing.md step 2 and the verify table to match.

Minor:
1. .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md "Gates run" · Minor.
   Issue: the template lists `ruff check src/ tests/`, `ruff format --check src/ tests/` and
   `mypy src/`. CI, CONTRIBUTING and README run `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and
   `mypy` with no paths. Those cover .github/scripts, and the mypy run covers the tests too.
   CONTRIBUTING says "CI runs the same checks". The checklist ticked on every PR checks less.
   Recommendation: use the same three commands, without paths.
2. Owner settings the first release needs, missing from BEAD-05's specification · Minor.
   This can only be settled by a live run.
   Issue: release.yml (header, lines 46-50) and releasing.md "The portal" both require two
   settings. The github-pages environment must allow deployments from tags v*, because
   GitHub creates it allowing the default branch only. horizon-vps must allow v* if it
   restricts deployment branches. BRIEF BEAD-05 and ht-30c name neither. Without the first,
   v1.0.0's portal-deploy is refused, after the deploy and the publish have already run.
   Recommendation: add both settings to BRIEF's BEAD-05 row and to ht-30c's description.
3. release.yml verify, the dispatch path (lines 22-25 and 103-107) · Minor.
   Issue: deploy.yml carried `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`, so a run from another
   branch never reached the host. release.yml has no equivalent. A dispatch "Use workflow

description: Spec: BRIEF.md BEAD-02

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
REVIEW PASSED: ht-kc1 (HT-005 BEAD-02). Range: 7992e96 and c418c42. Scope: .github/**, scripts/mutation.sh, .beadloom/flow.yml, tests/unit/deploy/**, RUNBOOK §7 (CI). Verdict: 0 Critical, 0 Major, 4 Minor, 3 Nitpick.

Channels: the review-brief withheld the bead comments, and I read none of the author's comments. The launch prompt named only the scope, the tools and the model repository. It carried no account of the change.

What was measured, all of it in a scratch clone at c418c42 with the project tree left untouched:
- actionlint v1.7.12 rc 0, and shellcheck deploy/*.sh scripts/*.sh rc 0.
- ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy src/ tests/ are clean. The adapter is also clean under ruff and mypy --strict when run by hand (see Minor 2).
- tests/unit/deploy: 150 passed. Full suite: 733 passed and 3 skipped (HT-004, named). Coverage 98.69%.
- beadloom ci on a clean index rc 0, and docs spaces --strict rc 0.
- Pins: git ls-remote resolves all four SHAs to the tags their comments name: checkout v7.0.1, setup-uv v10.3.0, cache v6.1.0, upload-artifact v7.0.2. beadloom 9.0.0 is on PyPI.
- Stage order: stage 2 needs all of stage 1, and ci-ok needs all five jobs with if: always(). There is no continue-on-error and no || true. Secrets enter only through env:, with no expression in any run: script, and the trigger is pull_request rather than pull_request_target. Every job has a timeout and contents: read. This matches BRIEF BEAD-01.
- scripts/mutation.sh, run for real:
  * Per change against origin/main: 34 functions, 243 mutants, 99.2%, rc 0, outcome scored.
  * A one-function commit (checkin_succeeded): exactly 4 mutants selected, all 4 killed.
  * A commit with no domain change: nothing-to-mutate, rc 0, with the reason given.
  * --min-score 100: rc 1, outcome scored, "Floor: 1.0 - the score is under it".
  * --sample 50 --seed 2026-W43: 100%, Wilson 95% interval 92.9-100%. Two runs drew identical name lists.

Bite tests (sabotage in the clone, removed by restoring the committed file there; the project tree was not touched):
- ci-ok if: success() -> red test_ci_ok_waits_for_every_other_job_and_runs_whatever_they_did.
- ci-ok counting only "failure" -> red test_ci_ok_is_red_and_names_the_job_that_did_not_succeed[cancelled] and [skipped].
- continue-on-error on the Ruff step -> red test_no_check_is_excused_from_failing_the_run[ci.yml].
- A tag pin in mutation.yml -> red test_every_action_is_pinned_...[mutation.yml] and test_one_action_is_pinned_to_one_commit_....
- tests needing only lint -> red test_stage_two_starts_only_after_all_of_stage_one[tests].
- beadloom-gate dropped from ci-ok's needs -> red test_ci_ok_waits_for_every_other_job....

Minor:
1. .github/workflows/ci.yml:205 (Coverage in the job summary), Minor. Issue: coverage report honours fail_under and exits 2 below the floor. Under set -euo pipefail the line total="$(uv run coverage report --format=total)" then aborts the step before anything reaches $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. I reproduced this with the step's script on below-floor data: rc 2 and no summary file. The step therefore writes no coverage line in exactly the run where the coverage figure matters most. The comment in test_coverage_is_kept_and_summarised_per_python ("A red pytest still reports its figure") does not hold for that case. Recommendation: use uv run coverage report --format=total --fail-under=0. I measured rc 0 and "20" on the same data. Add a test that runs the step on a .coverage below 80 and asserts the line was written.
2. .github/scripts/mutmut_adapter.py, Minor. Issue: CI runs ruff and mypy over src/ tests/ only, so the Python glue that decides which mutants are counted is linted and type-checked by no job. It passes both today only because I ran them by hand. Recommendation: add .github/scripts/ to the ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy lines, and to the assert_in_order strings in test_ci_workflow.py.
3. scripts/mutation.sh:121 and :182-189 (the verdict path), Minor. Issue: no test holds the script's exit code to beadloom's verdict. A shellcheck-clean sabotage, exit "$(( verdict * 0 ))", kept tests/unit/deploy at 150 passed. A real run with --min-score 100 then exited 0 while printing "the score is under it". Dividing the floor by 10000 in the awk line was also never caught. The two sabotages that did go red (exit 0, dropping --min-score) went red only through shellcheck SC2034, by accident. The Summary step reads only DIR/outcome, so it would not catch this either. The job is not required, which is why this is Minor. Recommendation: either have the Summary step fail on a "Floor: ... under it" line together with a nonzero exit, or test the script's tail with stub beadloom and uv executables on PATH (a stub beadloom exiting 1 on --stats must give script rc != 0, and one exiting 0 must give rc 0).
4. .github/workflows/ci.yml:39, Minor (the comment overstates). Issue: "every commit on main keeps a verdict". GitHub keeps at most one pending run per concurrency group whatever cancel-in-progress says, so a third quick push to main cancels the second push's pending CI. RUNBOOK §7 already says this about the deploy ("of several waiting, GitHub keeps the last one"). Recommendation: say "a running main CI is never cancelled; of several waiting, GitHub keeps the newest".

Nitpick:
- deploy.yml:216 (Deploy summary): if ssh fails mid-block, set -e exits inside the { } group. The ```text fence is left open in the summary, and the step adds a second red. The ssh config has no ConnectTimeout either, so an unreachable host costs the kernel's SYN timeout (~2 min) twice: preflight, then summary. Consider adding ConnectTimeout 15 to the vps host block.

API CHANGE (deploy contract, for ht-spa BEAD-09 workflows):
Units (source deploy/, installed to /etc/systemd/system/, mode 0644): horizon-checkin.service, horizon-checkin.timer, horizon-checkout.service, horizon-checkout.timer. Services: Type=oneshot, User=horizon, Group=horizon, WorkingDirectory=/opt/horizon-tracker, EnvironmentFile=/opt/horizon-tracker/.env, ExecStart=/opt/horizon-tracker/.venv/bin/horizon checkin|checkout, TimeoutStartSec=15min, After/Wants=network-online.target, no [Install] (started only by the timer). Timers: OnCalendar=*-*-* 07:55:00 Europe/Moscow / *-*-* 17:00:00 Europe/Moscow, Persistent=no, AccuracySec=1s, WantedBy=timers.target.
.env contract: /opt/horizon-tracker/.env, owner horizon:horizon, mode 0600, written by the deploy workflow on every deploy (e.g. install -m 600 -o horizon -g horizon). Secrets of Environment horizon-vps -> .env: HORIZON_USERNAME, HORIZON_PASSWORD, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID (VPS_HOST, VPS_USER, VPS_SSH_KEY, VPS_KNOWN_HOSTS are for ssh only). Non-secret values the workflow writes: HORIZON_URL=https://horizon.example.com/portal/webclient/, HORIZON_DESKTOP="DEV desktop", HT_TIMEZONE=Europe/Moscow, HT_CHECKIN_WINDOW=07:55-08:00, HT_CHECKOUT_WINDOW=17:00-17:05, HT_HOLD_SECONDS=120, HT_CHROME_PATH=/usr/bin/google-chrome, HT_ARTIFACTS_DIR=/opt/horizon-tracker/artifacts. Format is systemd EnvironmentFile, NOT shell: the workflow must write each value so systemd reads it literally (quotes, backslash, $ in the password); probe does not check the password, only checkin --force does.
Two obligations for BEAD-09 (stated in RUNBOOK §2.2 and §7): (1) restart the timers only if already enabled - use `systemctl try-restart horizon-checkin.timer horizon-checkout.timer`, NOT `restart`, which would START a disabled timer and switch the schedule on before the owner's manual run (PLAN BEAD-13); (2) smoke `horizon probe` as horizon with the same .env parser - e.g. `systemd-run --quiet --pipe --wait --collect --uid=horizon --gid=horizon --working-directory=/opt/horizon-tracker -p EnvironmentFile=/opt/horizon-tracker/.env /opt/horizon-tracker/.venv/bin/horizon probe` (RUNBOOK §3 uses exactly this as the `ht` helper).

What: deploy/horizon-{checkin,checkout}.{service,timer}, deploy/bootstrap.sh (0755), deploy/RUNBOOK.md (Russian).
Decisions:

- AccuracySec=1s on both timers: systemd's default 1 min accuracy may fire up to a minute late inside a 5-minute window.
- TimeoutStartSec=15min on both services (window 5 min + 120 s hold + teardown, with margin): a hung Chrome becomes a failed unit instead of blocking the next run. Noted in RUNBOOK §5: a timeout may produce no Telegram report.
- Services have no [Install]: only the timer starts them.
- HT_USER/HT_HOME are readonly in bootstrap (the units name them); HT_REPO, HT_CHROME_PATH, APT_PACKAGES overridable like the host's existing bootstrap. Chrome is checked right after the root check and before any change, never installed.
- `uv sync --locked` (production install fails on a stale lock instead of re-resolving).
- RUNBOOK manual runs use `systemd-run --uid=horizon -p EnvironmentFile=...` (helper `ht`), so manual runs read .env with the same parser as the timers; `source .env` in bash could mangle the password.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
API CHANGE (new infrastructure adapters, for BEAD-07 ht-oqx to wire in the CLI):

1. horizon_tracker.infrastructure.isdayoff.IsDayOffCalendar(client: httpx.Client) -- implements WorkingDayCalendar.is_working_day(day: date) -> bool | None. GET https://isdayoff.ru/YYYYMMDD with a per-request timeout of 5 s (TIMEOUT_SECONDS), independent of the client's own default. Body exactly "0"/"2" -> True, "1" -> False. httpx.HTTPError (any transport failure incl. timeouts), status != 200, or any other body (incl. "0\n", "", isdayoff codes 100/101/199) -> None, logged at WARNING on logger horizon_tracker.infrastructure.isdayoff, never raised.

2. horizon_tracker.infrastructure.telegram.TelegramNotifier(token: str, chat_id: str, client: httpx.Client) -- implements Notifier.send(report: RunReport) -> None.
   - report.screenshot is None -> POST bot<token>/sendMessage, form {chat_id, text=render(report)}.
   - report.screenshot set -> POST bot<token>/sendPhoto, multipart {chat_id, caption=render(report), photo=(file name, bytes)}; if the file cannot be read (OSError) or the Bot API refuses/fails the photo, it falls back to sendMessage with the same text, so the owner always gets the report text.
   - Per-request timeout 20 s (TIMEOUT_SECONDS), independent of the client default.
   - Any httpx.HTTPError or non-200 answer is logged at WARNING (method, status, Bot API "description", error type + redacted message) and swallowed: send never raises on delivery.
   - CONSTRUCTOR RAISES ValueError on a malformed token (must fullmatch \d+:[A-Za-z0-9_-]+ -- so a trailing newline or space from .env is refused) or an empty/blank chat_id; the message never echoes the value. The CLI should build the notifier at wiring time so a bad secret fails before the run, not mid-run. Strip nothing silently -- the CLI/config decides.
   - Token out of logs: the module logs no URL and redacts the token from error text and descriptions; on construction it attaches (once per process, idempotent) a logging.Filter to the "httpx" logger that masks api.telegram.org/bot<token> as bot<token>-placeholder in httpx's own INFO request lines. Records are never dropped. If the CLI configures logging, it need not silence httpx for the token's sake; httpcore's DEBUG lines carry no URL path.
   - chat_id never appears in my log records either (tested).
Both adapters take the httpx.Client from the caller and never close it: the CLI owns its lifetime (e.g. `with httpx.Client() as client:`).
Docs to check: docs/domains/infrastructure/README.md (lists "isdayoff.ru working-day calendar" and "Telegram notifier" as bullets; sync-check now flags it stale against isdayoff.py and telegram.py, hash_changed_since_head), RFC.md infrastructure table (telegram row: add the photo->text fallback and the 20 s timeout), PLAN BEAD-07 wiring.

comments.text:
API CHANGE (for BEAD-07 cli, ht-oqx): new public infrastructure API, commit 282811b.

horizon_tracker.infrastructure.config
- ConfigError(variable, problem): Exception; .variable = the env var name; str = "<VAR>: <problem>"; never carries a credential value.
- Settings (frozen dataclass), Settings.from_env(environ: Mapping[str, str]) -> Settings (pass os.environ; it is not read implicitly). Fields, in order:
  horizon_url: str            <- HORIZON_URL            REQUIRED (no default: deployment-specific, the RFC value is not baked into code)
  username: str               <- HORIZON_USERNAME       REQUIRED, credential (masked)
  password: str               <- HORIZON_PASSWORD       REQUIRED, credential (masked); value kept verbatim, not stripped
  desktop: str                <- HORIZON_DESKTOP        default "DEV desktop"
  telegram_token: str         <- TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN     REQUIRED, credential (masked)
  telegram_chat_id: str       <- TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID       REQUIRED, credential (masked); kept as str
  timezone: ZoneInfo          <- HT_TIMEZONE            default Europe/Moscow; unknown key -> ConfigError
  checkin_window: Window      <- HT_CHECKIN_WINDOW      default 07:55-08:00; strict HH:MM-HH:MM -> domain.schedule.Window
  checkout_window: Window     <- HT_CHECKOUT_WINDOW     default 17:00-17:05; start >= end -> ConfigError
  hold_seconds: int           <- HT_HOLD_SECONDS        default 120; non-negative whole number (0 allowed)
  chrome_path: Path           <- HT_CHROME_PATH         default /usr/bin/google-chrome
  artifacts_dir: Path         <- HT_ARTIFACTS_DIR       default /opt/horizon-tracker/artifacts
  Blank (whitespace-only) required var = missing; blank optional var = its default.
  repr/str/f-string render '***' for username, password, telegram_token, telegram_chat_id (CONTEXT lists the AD account and chat id as secrets too, so the mask is wider than "password and token").
  Constants exported: MASK, DEFAULT_* (one per optional variable).

horizon_tracker.infrastructure.clock
- SystemClock(tz: ZoneInfo): implements domain.ports.Clock. now() -> aware datetime in tz; sleep(seconds) -> time.sleep (negative raises ValueError).

horizon_tracker.infrastructure.artifacts
- RETENTION = timedelta(days=14)
- DirectoryArtifactStore(directory: Path, clock: Clock, retention: timedelta = RETENTION): implements domain.ports.ArtifactStore.
  screenshot_path(kind: RunKind) -> directory/"YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<kind>.png" by clock wall time; creates the directory, writes no file.
  prune() -> list[Path]: removes files named in that shape whose name time is strictly older than now - retention; foreign files, directories, malformed dates are left alone; absent directory -> []. NOT called implicitly: the CLI composition root should call store.prune() once per run (logs each removal at INFO).
  Same-second collision of the same kind overwrites (one screenshot per failed attempt, attempts are spaced by backoff).

comments.text:
API CHANGE (operator/CI surface, commit 7d68763): new .github/workflows/ci.yml (name "CI": pull_request->main, push->main, workflow_call; job `ci`) and .github/workflows/deploy.yml (name "Deploy": push->main, workflow_dispatch; job `gate` = uses ./.github/workflows/ci.yml; job `deploy` needs gate, if github.ref == 'refs/heads/main', environment horizon-vps, concurrency deploy-horizon-vps without cancel). Deploy step names: Set up SSH / Update the code / Build .env / Write .env / Install the units / Smoke: horizon probe / Remove the key and .env from the runner.
Deviations from RFC/PLAN text: (1) timers are `systemctl try-restart`, not `restart` (BEAD-08 contract; a restart would start a disabled timer); (2) the smoke is `systemd-run --quiet --pipe --wait --collect --uid=horizon --gid=horizon --working-directory=/opt/horizon-tracker -p EnvironmentFile=/opt/horizon-tracker/.env /opt/horizon-tracker/.venv/bin/horizon probe`, not `sudo -u horizon .../horizon probe` as the coordinator's brief said: the CLI reads only os.environ, so plain sudo -u sees no settings and would fail every deploy; (3) .env values are always double-quoted with \ " ` $ backslash-escaped (systemd's own write_env_var), so the file on the VPS differs in form, not in values, from the RUNBOOK §2.2 block; (4) checkout is `--detach <github.sha>` of the run, not a branch name.
Docs to check: RFC "Schedule and deploy" and PLAN BEAD-09 (say `systemctl restart` of the timers, `horizon probe` from horizon without naming how .env is read); RUNBOOK §2.2 says "Five variables — from the secrets above" but four come from secrets (HORIZON_USERNAME, HORIZON_PASSWORD, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID) - outside my section, left for the tech-writer; docs/services/cli.md "Used by" could name the deploy smoke; README if it describes CI.
